business_summary.text: Technology-driven affordable housing finance company lending to first-time home buyers, mainly families with monthly income under ₹50,000, across 13 states and union territories through 171 branches and 373 touchpoints.

call_points.text: Management is confident of delivering 25% AUM growth while keeping focus on profitability and portfolio quality.
Loans above ₹25 lakh rose to 18% of the portfolio from 14% a year earlier, a gradual shift management does not expect to compress spreads much.
Management does not expect a PLR cut, citing uncertainty from the West Asia crisis.
Capital adequacy was 42.6% with Tier 1 at 42.2%, down from 44.1% and 43.8% at Mar-2026.
The in-house AI platform 'Cue' is live, and bureau and bank-statement analysis models are in production; AI-led valuation and income analysis are in pilot.
CFO Nutan Gaba Patwari steps down effective August 31, 2026; the board is evaluating candidates.
Added 16 branches and 12 touchpoints in FY26, taking the network to 171 branches and 373 touchpoints.
64 more branches proposed, on top of 171 physical and 138 digital branches.
Q4FY26 disbursements hit an all-time high of ₹1,572 Cr, up 23.5% YoY and 19.3% QoQ.
GNPA at 1.8% (down 20 bps QoQ); 30+ DPD improved 50 bps QoQ to 3.2% and 1+ DPD 60 bps to 4.7%.
Liquidity buffer of ₹31,258 Mn at Mar'26; zero borrowing through commercial paper.

Home First Finance reported Q1FY27 results with AUM growth of 25.7% YoY to ₹16,938 Cr, disbursements of ₹1,628 Cr (+31.0% YoY), and PAT growth of 34.5% YoY to ₹160 Cr.
